score_1_desc: No dock scheduling exists - inbound trucks arrive whenever the vendor chooses, with no assigned time window and frequent dock congestion.
score_2_desc: A rough scheduling attempt exists (a phone call or message) but isn't tracked, and vendors regularly ignore it.
score_3_desc: A documented dock schedule with assigned time windows per vendor exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Dock scheduling is actively enforced with a booking system or calendar, and vendor adherence is tracked against a KPI.
score_5_desc: Dock scheduling is fully digitized (self-service vendor booking), with real-time visibility and automatic reflow when a slot is missed.

score_1_desc: No record of when inbound trucks actually arrive or when unloading finishes - there's no way to know how long anything sat at the dock.
score_2_desc: Arrival time is noted informally (a scrawled note) but not consistently, and isn't compiled anywhere.
score_3_desc: A documented process for logging arrival and unload-complete times exists and is generally followed, recorded manually or in a spreadsheet.
score_4_desc: Time-stamping is actively reviewed against a dock-to-shelf time KPI, with delays flagged and investigated.
score_5_desc: Time-stamping is automatic (system/scan-based) and dock-to-shelf time is a continuously monitored, benchmarked metric.

score_1_desc: No documented SOP for what happens between a truck arriving and produce reaching storage - the sequence depends entirely on whoever is working.
score_2_desc: An informal sequence is understood by experienced staff but isn't written down, and breaks down when they're absent.
score_3_desc: A documented dock-to-shelf SOP exists and is generally followed under normal conditions.
score_4_desc: SOP adherence is actively audited on a defined cadence, with deviations tracked and corrected.
score_5_desc: The SOP is system-guided (e.g. task prompts) and adherence is consistently near 100%, verified continuously.

score_1_desc: No written grading standard exists for any produce category - acceptance is a purely subjective call.
score_2_desc: A grading standard exists informally in a few people's heads but isn't written down anywhere.
score_3_desc: A documented grading rubric (ripeness, blemish tolerance, size) exists for major SKU categories.
score_4_desc: The grading rubric is actively maintained, covers most SKUs, and is referenced during training.
score_5_desc: Grading standards are documented with photo references for every SKU category and reviewed/updated on a regular cadence.

score_1_desc: Grading is applied inconsistently or not at all - different staff make different calls on the same produce.
score_2_desc: Grading happens but isn't sampling-based or systematic - whoever is at the dock eyeballs a few crates.
score_3_desc: A defined sampling method (e.g. check N crates per batch) is documented and generally followed.
score_4_desc: Sampling-based grading is actively tracked for consistency across shifts/staff, with outliers coached.
score_5_desc: Grading consistency is measured (e.g. inter-rater agreement) and continuously improved through training and feedback.

score_1_desc: Rejected produce is discarded or sent back with no record of quantity, reason, or vendor.
score_2_desc: Rejections are occasionally noted informally but not compiled or shared with vendors.
score_3_desc: A documented process for logging rejections (vendor, SKU, reason, quantity) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Rejection data is actively reviewed and shared with vendors on a defined cadence, feeding into vendor scorecards.
score_5_desc: Rejection data automatically feeds vendor performance reviews and sourcing decisions, with trends tracked over time.

score_1_desc: No batch or lot identification happens at receiving - once inside the facility, produce origin is untraceable.
score_2_desc: Batch/lot tagging happens manually and inconsistently (marker on a box), often illegible or lost.
score_3_desc: A documented batch-tagging process (vendor, date, lot) exists and is applied consistently.
score_4_desc: Batch tagging is actively verified at receiving with a defined accuracy target.
score_5_desc: Batch/lot identification is barcode/QR-based and system-captured at the point of receiving.

score_1_desc: Once a batch is put away, there's no way to trace it - stock is treated as a single undifferentiated pool.
score_2_desc: Some batches can be traced with effort (asking staff, checking notes) but it's unreliable.
score_3_desc: A documented process keeps batch identity associated with stock through storage, generally followed.
score_4_desc: Batch traceability through storage is actively spot-checked and discrepancies are investigated.
score_5_desc: Full batch-level traceability is system-enforced from receiving through storage to pick, queryable instantly.

score_1_desc: If a quality issue is found downstream, there's no way to trace it back to a specific inbound batch or vendor.
score_2_desc: Root-cause tracing is possible in theory but takes significant manual effort and often fails.
score_3_desc: A documented process exists to trace a downstream issue back to its batch/vendor, generally workable within a reasonable time.
score_4_desc: Traceability is actively tested/drilled on a defined cadence to confirm it actually works when needed.
score_5_desc: Any downstream issue can be traced to its exact inbound batch and vendor within minutes, system-supported.

score_1_desc: No temperature sensors installed anywhere in storage - conditions are assumed, never measured.
score_2_desc: A single sensor exists somewhere in the facility, not representative of conditions across different storage zones.
score_3_desc: Sensors are placed in each defined storage zone per a documented placement plan, generally followed.
score_4_desc: Sensor placement is actively reviewed against hot-spot/cold-spot mapping and adjusted when gaps are found.
score_5_desc: Sensor coverage is continuously validated (calibration checks, redundancy in critical zones) and placement is data-driven from historical temperature variance.

score_1_desc: Temperature is never logged - if it's checked at all, it's a glance with no record kept.
score_2_desc: Readings are taken irregularly and logged inconsistently, often skipped during busy periods.
score_3_desc: A documented reading schedule (e.g. every 2 hours) exists and logs are generally kept, manually or in a spreadsheet.
score_4_desc: Reading frequency is actively enforced with completion tracked against the schedule, gaps flagged.
score_5_desc: Readings are continuous and automatic (sensor-logged), with 100% time-coverage and no manual step required.

score_1_desc: No defined response when temperature goes out of range - it's noticed only if someone happens to check.
score_2_desc: An informal response exists ("tell the supervisor") but isn't documented or consistently followed.
score_3_desc: A documented escalation process (who's notified, what action is taken) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Escalations are actively tracked with response-time targets, and root causes of excursions are reviewed.
score_5_desc: Excursions trigger automatic real-time alerts with a defined SLA for response, and escalation effectiveness is continuously measured.

score_1_desc: No storage zones are defined at all - the facility is one undifferentiated space.
score_2_desc: Zones exist informally ("the cold corner") but aren't labeled or documented anywhere.
score_3_desc: Zones are documented and physically labeled, with a written guide for what belongs where.
score_4_desc: Zone definitions are actively reviewed and refined based on operational experience, with staff trained on them.
score_5_desc: Zone layout is data-optimized (temperature mapping, produce mix) and digitally referenced in the WMS.

score_1_desc: No awareness of ethylene sensitivity - gas-producing and gas-sensitive produce are stored together routinely, accelerating spoilage.
score_2_desc: Ethylene sensitivity is known informally by some staff but not applied systematically.
score_3_desc: A documented ethylene-compatibility guide exists and separation is generally practiced.
score_4_desc: Ethylene separation is actively audited and violations are tracked back to spoilage outcomes.
score_5_desc: Ethylene management is systematized (zone assignment enforces it automatically) and continuously validated against spoilage data.

score_1_desc: Produce is put away wherever there's space, regardless of defined zones.
score_2_desc: Staff generally know where things should go but zoning isn't checked or enforced.
score_3_desc: A documented put-away process references zone assignment and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Zone compliance at put-away is actively spot-checked, with misplacement tracked and corrected.
score_5_desc: Zone assignment is system-enforced at put-away (WMS blocks incorrect placement).

score_1_desc: No humidity targets exist for any zone - humidity is whatever it happens to be.
score_2_desc: A rough humidity preference exists informally but isn't documented or measured against.
score_3_desc: Documented humidity targets exist per zone/produce category and are referenced.
score_4_desc: Humidity is actively measured against targets with corrective action when out of range.
score_5_desc: Humidity targets are continuously refined based on spoilage outcomes and automatically enforced per zone.

score_1_desc: No ventilation equipment maintenance - fans/humidifiers run (or don't) with no upkeep plan.
score_2_desc: Equipment is fixed reactively only after visible failure, with no preventive maintenance.
score_3_desc: A documented maintenance schedule exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Maintenance completion is actively tracked against the schedule, with equipment downtime monitored.
score_5_desc: Maintenance is predictive/condition-based, with equipment performance continuously monitored and downtime near zero.

score_1_desc: Slotting ignores sales velocity entirely - fast and slow movers are placed identically, with no regard to picker travel time.
score_2_desc: Fast movers are placed conveniently based on staff habit, not documented or data-driven.
score_3_desc: A documented slotting plan based on velocity tiers exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Slot assignment is actively reviewed against current velocity data on a defined cadence and adjusted.
score_5_desc: Slotting is dynamically optimized by an algorithm/system recommendation based on real-time velocity.

score_1_desc: Placement ignores shelf-life entirely - short-life items can end up in the slowest-to-reach locations.
score_2_desc: Shelf-life is considered informally by experienced staff but not systematically.
score_3_desc: A documented placement rule links shelf-life to proximity (shortest-life nearest pack-out) and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Shelf-life-aware placement is actively audited and adjusted based on spoilage patterns.
score_5_desc: Placement is system-recommended based on live shelf-life data per batch.

score_1_desc: No time-to-shelf target exists - produce can sit unshelved for an unpredictable, untracked duration.
score_2_desc: A rough expectation exists informally but isn't measured.
score_3_desc: A documented time-to-shelf target exists and is occasionally checked.
score_4_desc: Time-to-shelf is actively measured against the target with delays investigated.
score_5_desc: Time-to-shelf is continuously tracked in real time and benchmarked against a best-in-class threshold.

score_1_desc: Staffing doesn't flex with inbound volume at all - peak periods cause the same delays every time with no adjustment.
score_2_desc: Staffing is adjusted informally and inconsistently when someone notices a backlog.
score_3_desc: A documented staffing plan for peak inbound periods exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Staffing response is actively reviewed against actual peak performance and refined.
score_5_desc: Staffing is dynamically planned using inbound forecast data, with peak delays minimized proactively.

score_1_desc: No date labeling on bins or locations - there's no way to tell which stock is older without digging through it.
score_2_desc: Some batches are dated informally (marker on a box) but inconsistently.
score_3_desc: A documented date-labeling process exists and is generally applied.
score_4_desc: Date-labeling accuracy is actively spot-checked and corrected.
score_5_desc: Date labeling is barcode/system-based and automatically visible at the point of pick.

score_1_desc: Pickers grab whichever unit is easiest to reach, with no regard to which batch is older.
score_2_desc: FEFO is understood informally but frequently skipped under time pressure.
score_3_desc: A documented FEFO picking process exists and is generally followed with spot checks.
score_4_desc: FEFO adherence is actively audited on a schedule, with violations tracked and coached.
score_5_desc: FEFO is system-directed at pick (the WMS routes pickers to the oldest eligible batch) with adherence near 100%.

score_1_desc: No shelf-life is recorded per batch - there's no way to know how close any given unit is to expiry.
score_2_desc: Shelf-life is estimated by appearance rather than recorded from receipt date.
score_3_desc: A documented shelf-life standard per SKU (days from receipt) is defined and used to track batches.
score_4_desc: Remaining shelf-life is actively tracked per batch and reviewed on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Shelf-life is tracked per batch in a system that computes remaining life automatically from receipt date.

score_1_desc: Aging stock is only noticed once it's visibly spoiling - no proactive flagging happens at all.
score_2_desc: Aging stock is occasionally noticed informally but no consistent action is taken.
score_3_desc: A documented process flags aging stock at a defined threshold and prescribes an action (markdown, priority pick).
score_4_desc: Aging-stock flags are actively actioned and tracked to completion, with outcomes reviewed.
score_5_desc: Aging stock is automatically flagged and routed (markdown, redistribution, priority pick) with no manual step.

score_1_desc: No cycle counting happens - stock records and physical stock are never reconciled until a pick fails.
score_2_desc: Counts happen occasionally and informally with no defined schedule or coverage.
score_3_desc: A documented cycle-count schedule (e.g. weekly per zone) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Count completion is actively tracked against the schedule with coverage gaps flagged.
score_5_desc: Cycle counting is continuous/perpetual, system-driven, with full SKU coverage on a rolling basis.

score_1_desc: Count variances are recorded (if at all) with no investigation into why they happened.
score_2_desc: Variances are occasionally looked into informally, without a consistent process.
score_3_desc: A documented variance-investigation process exists and is generally followed for significant variances.
score_4_desc: Variance root causes are actively tracked and trends reviewed to prevent recurrence.
score_5_desc: Variance investigation is systematic and data-driven, with root-cause patterns feeding process improvements automatically.

score_1_desc: Replenishment is purely reactive - triggered only after a stockout is noticed.
score_2_desc: A rough par level exists informally but isn't consistently used to trigger replenishment.
score_3_desc: A documented par level/trigger threshold exists per SKU category and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Trigger thresholds are actively reviewed against sell-through data and adjusted.
score_5_desc: Replenishment triggers are dynamically calculated from real-time sell-through and shelf-life data.

score_1_desc: Replenishment doesn't adjust for known demand spikes at all - promotions and peak periods cause the same stockouts every time.
score_2_desc: Adjustments happen informally and inconsistently when someone remembers an upcoming promotion.
score_3_desc: A documented process adjusts replenishment ahead of known demand drivers and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Peak/promo adjustments are actively reviewed post-event for accuracy and refined.
score_5_desc: Demand-driver adjustments are modeled and applied automatically based on historical promo/peak performance.

score_1_desc: No real sales data feeds the order quantity - it's guessed or copied from the last order.
score_2_desc: Recent sales are referenced informally but not systematically incorporated.
score_3_desc: A documented forecasting input (recent sales trend) is used consistently.
score_4_desc: Forecast inputs are actively validated for quality and expanded to include more signals (weather, day-of-week).
score_5_desc: Forecast inputs are comprehensive and automatically ingested (sales, seasonality, promotions, external signals).

score_1_desc: Forecast accuracy is never checked - there's no feedback loop between predicted and actual demand.
score_2_desc: Accuracy is occasionally noticed informally when a big miss happens.
score_3_desc: A documented review cadence compares forecast to actuals and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Forecast accuracy is actively tracked as a KPI, with systematic adjustments based on error patterns.
score_5_desc: Forecast accuracy is continuously monitored with automated model refinement based on error trends.

score_1_desc: Stockouts aren't tracked at all - it's unclear which SKUs or times are most affected.
score_2_desc: Stockouts are noticed anecdotally but not measured.
score_3_desc: A documented stockout rate is tracked at a basic level per SKU category.
score_4_desc: Stockout rate is actively monitored against a target, with root causes reviewed.
score_5_desc: Stockout rate is tracked in real time per SKU/store with automated root-cause tagging.

score_1_desc: Overstock and the spoilage it causes are never connected - they're treated as unrelated problems.
score_2_desc: The link is occasionally noticed informally but not tracked.
score_3_desc: A documented process tracks spoilage attributable to overstock at a basic level.
score_4_desc: Overstock-linked spoilage is actively monitored and used to adjust replenishment parameters.
score_5_desc: Overstock and spoilage are jointly optimized in a single system view, continuously tuned to minimize both.

score_1_desc: No weighing equipment exists for loose/weighted produce - quantities are estimated by eye.
score_2_desc: Some weighing equipment exists but isn't consistently used or calibrated.
score_3_desc: A documented weighing process with calibrated scales exists at defined stations and is generally used.
score_4_desc: Scale calibration and usage are actively audited on a schedule.
score_5_desc: Weighing is integrated into the pick workflow (system-connected scales) with calibration continuously monitored.

score_1_desc: No tolerance standard exists for weighted picks - over/under-fulfillment is common and unmeasured.
score_2_desc: A rough tolerance is understood informally but not enforced or measured.
score_3_desc: A documented tolerance band exists per SKU and is generally referenced.
score_4_desc: Tolerance adherence is actively measured against a KPI, with deviations tracked to individual pickers.
score_5_desc: Tolerance is system-verified at pack (automatic flag on out-of-tolerance) with accuracy consistently best-in-class.

score_1_desc: No packaging standard exists - packaging choice is left entirely to whoever is packing.
score_2_desc: A rough packaging preference exists for a few fragile items but isn't documented.
score_3_desc: A documented packaging standard per produce category exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Packaging standards are actively reviewed against damage data and refined.
score_5_desc: Packaging is continuously optimized per SKU based on transit-damage analytics.

score_1_desc: Transit damage isn't tracked - complaints or returns are handled case by case with no pattern analysis.
score_2_desc: Damage is occasionally noted informally but not compiled.
score_3_desc: A documented process logs transit damage (SKU, cause) and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Damage data is actively reviewed and fed back into packaging decisions on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Damage tracking is real-time and automatically triggers packaging standard updates.

score_1_desc: Spoiled produce is discarded with no record of quantity, SKU, or cause at all.
score_2_desc: Spoilage is estimated informally rather than logged consistently.
score_3_desc: A documented logging process (SKU, quantity, reason) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Spoilage logging completeness is actively audited and gaps are corrected.
score_5_desc: Spoilage is logged in real time per SKU/batch with automated reporting.

score_1_desc: There's no shrinkage percentage calculated at all - spoilage cost is invisible.
score_2_desc: Shrinkage is estimated roughly but not calculated as a consistent percentage of throughput.
score_3_desc: Shrinkage % is calculated on a defined cadence and compared to a basic target.
score_4_desc: Shrinkage % is actively tracked as a KPI and reviewed against a best-in-class benchmark.
score_5_desc: Shrinkage % is tracked in real time and directly feeds sourcing/replenishment decisions.

score_1_desc: Spoilage causes are never categorized - it's treated as an unavoidable cost, not a solvable problem.
score_2_desc: Causes are occasionally guessed at informally.
score_3_desc: A documented categorization (over-order, cold-chain break, aged stock, damage) exists and is generally applied.
score_4_desc: Cause categorization is actively analyzed for patterns and reviewed on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Cause categorization is systematic and data-driven, with patterns surfaced automatically.

score_1_desc: No corrective actions are taken based on spoilage causes - the same problems recur unaddressed.
score_2_desc: Corrective actions are occasionally taken informally but not tracked to completion.
score_3_desc: A documented process assigns and tracks corrective actions for identified causes.
score_4_desc: Corrective action effectiveness is actively measured and reviewed.
score_5_desc: Corrective actions are automatically prioritized by impact and their effectiveness is tracked continuously.

score_1_desc: Stock disappears from the floor with no formal write-off, approval, or verification at all.
score_2_desc: Write-offs are recorded informally and inconsistently, often without approval.
score_3_desc: A documented write-off SOP (verification, approval) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Write-off approvals are actively audited for compliance with the SOP.
score_5_desc: Write-off approval is system-integrated and fully auditable, with no manual gaps.

score_1_desc: Disposed stock is never reconciled against inventory records - the system and reality drift apart silently.
score_2_desc: Reconciliation happens occasionally and informally.
score_3_desc: A documented reconciliation process runs on a defined cadence and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Reconciliation is actively monitored for unusual patterns, which are investigated.
score_5_desc: Reconciliation is automatic and real-time, with disposal method also optimized (e.g. donation/composting) to reduce cost and waste impact.
